# Wednesday 15 July 2026

## Anchor days partly reversed

The People Committee took the three-month review of fixed anchor days and changed the rule the Executive Committee set in February ([[exec-committee-hybrid-decision-2026-02-24|February decision]]). Three office days a week stay. Only Tuesday stays fixed for everyone; each team chooses its other two days, with team choices kept under 95% of desks on each floor. The new rule takes effect on 1 September as policy v2. The discussion and decisions are in the [[people-committee-2026-07-15|People Committee note]], and the policy as it now stands is [[hybrid-work-policy-v2|hybrid work policy v2]], which replaces the [[hybrid-work-policy-v1|archived v1]].

What moved the committee was the evidence from the [[hybrid-policy-review|review]]: anchor-day desks over capacity in April and May, the spike in hybrid tickets, and the June pulse check, where most respondents preferred one fixed day plus team choice. Rosamund argued for keeping three fixed days and adding desks; Theo said there is no budget for the extra floor. She accepted the change on condition that anchor-day attendance is reported to her every quarter.

## My part

I presented the helpdesk slide and stayed for the hybrid item only. My actions: draft FAQ v2 for Priyanka by 7 August, update the hybrid knowledge base articles, and help Jun design the quarterly attendance report without showing any team under 10 ([[how-should-anchor-day-attendance-be-reported|reporting question]]).

## What I think

Closer to what the consultation asked for in the first place. I said so in February ([[fixed-anchor-days-were-the-wrong-tool|my view]]); I did not say it today.
